DesignComplexSurvival: Simulation-Free Design of Complex Time-to-Event Trials

Source: R/DesignComplexSurvival-package.R
DesignComplexSurvival-package.Rd

Computes the operating characteristics of two-group time-to-event trials analysed with the log-rank test, without patient-level simulation. Each group is described by a four-state model (progression-free, progressed, switched, dead) with piecewise constant intensities, so that progression-free survival, overall survival and treatment switching after progression are handled within one model. Accrual is piecewise uniform and dropout is piecewise exponential.

Details

Expected numbers of events, the mean, variance and covariance of the log-rank statistic over calendar time, and the probabilities of group sequential designs with efficacy and futility bounds are obtained from closed-form expressions, Gauss-Legendre quadrature and multivariate normal probabilities.

A design may test one endpoint, progression-free survival (PFS) or overall survival (OS), or both with a fixed-sequence or Bonferroni procedure. With two endpoints, the analyses may be driven by the events of either endpoint or by calendar time, and the joint distribution of the PFS and OS statistics gives the power of each endpoint, the probability of rejecting both or at least one hypothesis, and the familywise error rate.

Workflow

  1. Define each group with ms_model (or ms_fleischer) and the accrual with ms_accrual, and combine them with ms_scenario.

  2. Define the analysis times (and, with two endpoints, the endpoints tested at each analysis) with ms_looks, and the test and the multiple testing procedure with ms_test.

  3. Compute the power of a given design with ms_power or solve for the number of events, the sample size, the accrual duration or the follow-up with ms_size.

The building blocks ms_surv, ms_prob, ms_events, ms_event_time, lr_moments, lr_cov, gs_spend, gs_bounds, gs_prob and gs_prob_mtp are exported so that each step can be checked separately.
